stages.name: Other kingdoms
stages.desc: Media, Lydia, Cilicia and other powers outside the struggle

stages.name: Egyptian
stages.desc: Ruled or held by the pharaohs of Sais

stages.name: Babylonian
stages.desc: Ruled by Babylon or by its vassal kings

stages.name: Tyrian & Phoenician
stages.desc: Independent Phoenician city-states led by Tyre

stages.name: Cypriot kingdoms
stages.desc: Independent Greek and Phoenician city-kingdoms of Cyprus

stages.name: Greek Cyrenaica
stages.desc: Cyrene and the Greek cities of Libya

stages.name: Persian
stages.desc: The empire of Cyrus and Cambyses

states.name: Cyprus
timeline: About ten city-kingdoms, Greek and Phoenician: Salamis, Paphos, Kition, Amathus and others
Cypriot ships fight beside Tyre and are beaten at sea by Apries' fleet
Amasis conquers Cyprus and makes its kings pay tribute (date approximate)
The Cypriot kings go over to Persia and put their ships at Cambyses' service

states.name: Israel
timeline: Judah's lowland forts and the Philistine coast, Babylonian vassals; Judah rebels under Zedekiah
Babylon besieges Lachish and Azekah; the Lachish letters ask for help from Egypt
Passes to Cyrus with the fall of Babylon

states.name: Palestine
timeline: Judah's hill country and Gaza; King Zedekiah stops paying tribute to Babylon
Jerusalem and its temple are destroyed; Judah becomes a Babylonian province
Passes to Cyrus with the fall of Babylon
Cyrus allows the Judean exiles to return and rebuild the temple

states.name: Lebanon
timeline: Tyre, Sidon, Byblos and Arwad: Babylonian vassals, restless and courting Egypt
Nebuchadnezzar begins a thirteen-year siege of island Tyre
Apries storms Sidon and the coastal towns submit to Egypt (date approximate)
Tyre comes to terms with Babylon; Egypt's foothold on the coast is lost
Tyre's kings are removed; judges govern the city under Babylon
Hiram III, held in Babylon, returns to rule Tyre
The Phoenician cities pass to Cyrus with the fall of Babylon

states.name: Syria
timeline: Babylonian since Carchemish in 605; Riblah serves as Nebuchadnezzar's headquarters
Passes to Cyrus with the fall of Babylon

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Lydia in the west, Cilicia in the south, the Medes in the east
After the Battle of the Eclipse, the Halys river becomes Lydia's border with Media
Neriglissar of Babylon campaigns in rough Cilicia
Cyrus defeats Croesus and takes Sardis; Ionia follows

states.name: Libya
timeline: Cyrene under Battus II invites new Greek settlers; Libyan peoples hold most of the land
Cyrene destroys the Egyptian army sent to help the Libyans at Irasa
Peace with Amasis, sealed by his marriage to Ladice of Cyrene

states.name: Iraq
timeline: Babylon of Nebuchadnezzar II, the greatest city of its age
Nebuchadnezzar dies; three kings rule in six years
Nabonidus takes the throne
Cyrus defeats the Babylonians at Opis and enters Babylon

states.name: Iran
timeline: The kingdom of the Medes; the Persians of Anshan are their vassals
Cyrus becomes king of Anshan, still a Median vassal
Cyrus overthrows Astyages and takes Ecbatana: the Persian empire is born

states.name: Jordan
timeline: Ammon, Moab and Edom, Babylonian vassals; Ammon joins the plotting against Babylon
Nebuchadnezzar's army campaigns against Ammon and Moab
Nabonidus campaigns in Edom on his way to Arabia
Passes to Cyrus with the fall of Babylon

states.name: Egypt
timeline: Apries (Wahibre) succeeds Psamtik II at Sais, with Greek and Carian mercenaries and a war fleet
Apries sends an army into Judah to relieve besieged Jerusalem
The army revolts after Irasa and proclaims Amasis pharaoh; Apries' mercenaries lose at Momemphis
Babylon invades in support of Apries; Apries is killed and Amasis holds the throne
Amasis dies after forty-four years; Psamtik III faces Persia alone

events.title: Apries crowned
events.text: Apries, called Hophra in the Bible, succeeds his father Psamtik II at the Delta capital of Sais.

events.title: Siege of Jerusalem
events.text: Nebuchadnezzar's army surrounds Jerusalem after King Zedekiah of Judah rebels, counting on Egypt.

events.title: Egypt marches north
events.text: An Egyptian army enters the south of Judah and the Babylonians briefly lift the siege of Jerusalem.

events.title: Lachish letters
events.text: Ostraca from Lachish record a Judean commander going down to Egypt as the Babylonians close in.

events.title: Zedekiah at Riblah
events.text: The fleeing king of Judah is captured and blinded at Nebuchadnezzar's headquarters in Syria.

events.title: Jerusalem burned
events.text: The Babylonians burn Jerusalem and its temple and deport much of Judah's population.

events.title: Flight to Egypt
events.text: After the murder of the governor Gedaliah, Judean refugees with the prophet Jeremiah settle at Tahpanhes.

events.title: Battle of the Eclipse
events.text: A solar eclipse halts a battle between Lydians and Medes; peace makes the Halys their border.

events.title: Siege of Tyre
events.text: Nebuchadnezzar begins a thirteen-year siege of Tyre, safe on its island behind its walls and fleet.

events.title: Ammon and Moab
events.text: A Babylonian army campaigns against Ammon and Moab and deports more people from Judah.

events.title: Ishtar Gate
events.text: Babylon's glazed blue gate of lions, bulls and dragons crowns Nebuchadnezzar's rebuilding of the city.

events.title: Apries takes Sidon
events.text: Diodorus says Apries stormed Sidon and frightened the other Phoenician towns into submission.

events.title: Battle at sea
events.text: Apries' fleet defeats the ships of Tyre and Cyprus in a great sea battle off the Phoenician coast.

events.title: Tyre submits
events.text: After thirteen years Tyre comes to terms with Babylon; its king is replaced.

events.title: Ezekiel's oracle
events.text: Among the exiles in Babylonia, Ezekiel declares that Nebuchadnezzar, unpaid at Tyre, will be given Egypt.

events.title: Libyans call Egypt
events.text: The Libyan king Adicran, losing land to Cyrene's new Greek settlers, asks Apries for help.

events.title: Disaster at Irasa
events.text: The Greeks of Cyrene destroy Apries' native Egyptian army near the spring of Thestes.

events.title: The army revolts
events.text: The survivors accuse Apries of sending them to die; the general Amasis, sent to calm them, is proclaimed king.

events.title: Battle of Momemphis
events.text: Amasis' Egyptian warriors defeat Apries' Carian and Ionian mercenaries in the western Delta.

events.title: Babylon invades Egypt
events.text: A Babylonian tablet records Nebuchadnezzar's campaign against Amasis in his thirty-seventh year.

events.title: Apries killed
events.text: Apries dies trying to win back his throne; Amasis buries him with honour at Sais.

events.title: Ladice of Cyrene
events.text: Amasis makes peace with Cyrene and marries a Greek noblewoman, Ladice.

events.title: Naukratis
events.text: Amasis makes Naukratis the trading city where Greek merchants may settle and build temples.

events.title: Judges of Tyre
events.text: Tyre's kings are removed and judges govern the city for several years under Babylon.

events.title: Nebuchadnezzar dies
events.text: After forty-three years, the conqueror of Jerusalem dies; Babylon falls into court intrigue.

events.title: Amasis takes Cyprus
events.text: Amasis is the first, says Herodotus, to conquer Cyprus and make it pay tribute.

events.title: Cyrus of Anshan
events.text: Cyrus becomes king of the Persians of Anshan, a vassal of the Median king Astyages.

events.title: Neriglissar in Cilicia
events.text: The Babylonian king campaigns in rough Cilicia, burning towns along the coast.

events.title: Nabonidus at Tayma
events.text: Nabonidus leaves his son Belshazzar in Babylon and spends ten years at the Arabian oasis of Tayma.

events.title: Hiram III
events.text: Tyre's last king of the Babylonian age returns from captivity in Babylon.

events.title: Ecbatana falls
events.text: The Median army deserts Astyages; Cyrus takes Ecbatana and the Median empire.

events.title: Pact with Croesus
events.text: Croesus of Lydia, Amasis, Babylon and Sparta draw together against the rising Persian power.

events.title: Gift to Delphi
events.text: Amasis gives a thousand talents of alum toward rebuilding Apollo's burned temple at Delphi.

events.title: Sardis falls
events.text: Cyrus defeats Croesus and takes his capital; Egyptian troops are said to have fought for Lydia.

events.title: Ionia conquered
events.text: Persian armies take the Greek cities of Ionia; the Phocaeans sail away rather than submit.

events.title: Battle of Opis
events.text: Cyrus defeats the Babylonian army on the Tigris.

events.title: Babylon falls
events.text: Persian troops enter Babylon in October; Syria, Phoenicia and Judah pass to Cyrus.

events.title: Return from exile
events.text: Cyrus allows the Judean exiles to go home and rebuild the temple in Jerusalem.

events.title: Polycrates of Samos
events.text: Amasis' ally Polycrates builds a fleet of a hundred warships; later he will send ships to Persia.

events.title: Cyrus dies
events.text: Cyrus is killed in Central Asia and buried at Pasargadae; his son Cambyses turns toward Egypt.

events.title: Evelthon's spindle
events.text: Asked for an army by the exiled queen of Cyrene, Evelthon of Salamis sends her a golden spindle instead.

events.title: Phanes defects
events.text: Phanes, a Greek captain of Amasis' mercenaries, flees to Cambyses with Egypt's secrets.

events.title: Water for Sinai
events.text: Cambyses arranges with an Arab king to carry water for his army across the desert road to Egypt.

events.title: Amasis dies
events.text: Amasis dies after forty-four years on the throne, months before the Persian army reaches Egypt.

events.title: Cyprus changes sides
events.text: The kings of Cyprus give themselves to the Persians and add their ships to Cambyses' fleet.

eras: Apries and the Siege of Tyre
chartNote: Share of the area of eleven present-day countries, by the power that held most of each one. Regions are today's boundaries and the categories are a simplification: Libya stands for Greek Cyrenaica, Turkey for Lydia, Cilicia and Media, and Iran for Media and Persia. Some dates, such as Apries' Phoenician campaign and Amasis' conquest of Cyprus, are approximate.
